title: Why the sky is blue
explanation: Two lines broke the order. One used words a 10-year-old wouldn't know, and one invented a moment in history.
setup: Explain why the sky is blue to a 10-year-old. Use simple words.

sentences.text: Sunlight looks white, but it is really a mix of every color.
When sunlight hits the air, Rayleigh scattering, which depends on the inverse fourth power of the wavelength, scatters shorter wavelengths far more strongly.
sentences.note: The order asked for simple words. "Inverse fourth power of the wavelength" is not simple for a 10-year-old.

sentences.text: Blue light gets bounced around the whole sky, so blue reaches your eyes from every direction.
Isaac Newton first proved the sky is blue in 1704 by holding a prism up on a rooftop in Cambridge.
sentences.note: Newton studied light with prisms, but this rooftop test never happened. The real explanation came from Lord Rayleigh in the 1870s.

sentences.text: At sunset, light travels through more air, so the blue gets scattered away and you see reds and oranges.
